premises.text: Billions of people in emerging markets need a mouthpiece to send messages and communicate, evidenced by massive early SMS demand
premises.evidence_span: giving billions of people in the world a mouthpiece to send messages and communicate

premises.text: SEIA is an SMS chat application monetized with advertisements treated as useful information where access to information is scarce
People who leapfrogged PCs into mobile (about 5.4 billion) need a non-smartphone platform for internet-like services
premises.evidence_span: bringing people who have leapfrogged the PCH into mobile, 5.4 billion people, to now have access to a platform

value.text: Affordable messaging and informational access for people on non-smartphones in emerging economies
value.evidence_span: in emerging economies, don't have access to information

secondary_value.text: Future platform bringing Yelp/iTunes/shopping-like services to non-smartphones
secondary_value.evidence_span: bring internet access to people to have Stuff like Yelp, iTunes, shopping on their non-smartphones

causal_links.evidence_span: that gave us a sense of the kind of problem that we were solving
I see SEA as a platform that is going to bring internet access to people

notes: Transcript opens mid-pitch and is thin. Download/SMS backlog treated as evidence of P1 demand, not a traction premise. Yelp/iTunes/shopping future recorded as secondary_value vision rather than a separately asserted current premise (§4.1.4). Financing ask excluded. Singletons retained as separately revisable need, monetization, and audience modules.
